note: Living content ledger for NRITOUSA.com. THIS FILE IS THE HAND-MAINTAINED PART — the backlog of content work we know about. Everything else in the rendered ledger (link health, meta stats, verified-number status, the Fast Answer coverage gap) is regenerated from the audit scripts each run, so it can never drift from reality. Regenerate with `npm run ledger` (needs a prior `next build`). Add an item when an audit surfaces work we are not doing today; move it to status:done with a `resolved` date when it ships. Do not delete resolved items — the log is the record of what changed and when.

items.title: 79 high-intent pages still lack the verified-numbers treatment
items.detail: audit:intent-numbers scores every route that answers a number question against six affordances: a Fast Answer block, a numeric estimate, a last-verified stamp, an official-source link, FAQ schema, and an Article dateModified. 79 High-priority pages are missing at least one. The H-1B lottery cluster is the weakest — most of those pages have FAQ schema and nothing else, so they make numeric claims with no stamp and no citation.

items.title: 14 verified-number stamps are past the 45-day threshold
items.detail: Was 21 on 2026-09-02. Seven were re-confirmed against their official sources that day and bumped: I-90 online ($415) and paper ($465) fees, the no-separate-biometrics-fee line, the $120 Affidavit of Support review fee, the $325 family-based IV fee, the $10,000 FBAR threshold and the 10% early-withdrawal penalty. No value was found to have actually drifted — the stamps lag, the numbers were right. The remaining 14 are prose/range values (processing times, passport windows, FBAR deadline, FATCA, SS credits, FAFSA) plus the employment-based ($345) and other ($205) IV fees, none of which a script can check.

items.title: PWD planning band (4–8 months) now runs ahead of DOL's own queue
items.detail: permProcessingData.ts plans prevailing-wage determinations at 4–8 months. DOL FLAG's receipt months imply faster: OEWS PERM cases filed April 2026 were being processed as of 30 June (~2–3 months), non-OEWS March 2026 (~3–4). The stored receipt months match DOL exactly, so the underlying data is right — it is the derived band whose floor sits above observed reality. Defensible as a buffer while DOL's PWD table is itself seven weeks stale, but it is the one figure where we tell readers to expect worse than they will likely get. Resolved 2026-09-15: refreshed against the FLAG dashboard as of Aug 31, 2026 — PWD is at May 2026 receipts for both wage sources and the published PERM average is 336 days, so the bands moved to 3–6 (PWD) and 10–14 (analyst review) months, with the derived totals following. siteWideVerifiedNumbers was updated in step and verifiedNumbers.consistency.test.ts held the two files together.
items.nextStep: Re-check flag.dol.gov/processingtimes when DOL refreshes the PWD table; if the receipt months hold, drop pwdPlanningMonthsLow to 3.

items.title: 223 titles exceed the SERP display limit
items.detail: Median indexable title is 64 characters; 223 exceed 60 and 63 exceed 80, topping out at 95. Google rewrites rather than penalises, so this is not an error — but the tail is where the keyword differentiators sit, and on a 95-character title the tail is always cut. Worst offenders are the long descriptive titles on /articles/real-estate-first-investment-immigrants, /can-h1b-parents-open-trump-account-for-child and /india-business-visa-from-usa.
items.nextStep: Trim to ~57 chars before the ' | NRI to USA' template, front-loading the keyword. Batch by cluster so sibling titles stay parallel.

items.title: 152 meta descriptions exceed 160 characters
items.detail: Median is 154 characters, but 152 pages exceed 160 and 34 exceed 200, with a 310-character outlier on /india-investments/should-nris-keep-investments-in-india. Long descriptions are simply truncated in the SERP; the risk is that the sentence carrying the click argument is the one cut.
items.nextStep: Rewrite the 34 pages over 200 characters first — below that the loss is marginal.

items.title: 30 outbound citations can only ever be verified by hand

USCIS silently retired five paths before the 2026-08-18 audit caught them, and those were only visible because www.uscis.gov happens to answer 404 rather than 403.

items.title: OPT-denial grace period — RESOLVED against the USCIS Policy Manual
items.detail: Resolved 2026-08-20. USCIS Policy Manual Vol.2 Pt.F Ch.5: an initial post-completion OPT denial leaves F-1 status expiring 60 days from the program end date or the denial date, WHICHEVER IS LATER — except where the denial was for failure to maintain status, in which case immediate departure is expected. A STEM extension denied after the OPT EAD expired ends status 60 days from the denial date. All three branches are now encoded in optDenialRules and rendered on the OPT calculator, with tests.

Do NOT simplify this to 'the fee expires on Sept 20' — expiry and vacatur are independent, and either could change first.

items.title: EAD cluster still explained the repealed 540-day auto-extension in the present tense
items.detail: A DHS interim final rule (90 FR 48799) effective Oct 30, 2025 ended the automatic extension of work authorization for timely-filed I-765 renewals, and it is still in force as of Sep 2026 (APA suits pending, no injunction). eadProcessingData.ts had been updated and the tools were correct, but the page prose had not: /ead-renewal-gap's FAQs described 'currently up to 540 days' and 'documents your employer needs during the extension', and /ead-processing-time told readers USCIS had increased the extension to 540 days. Readers were being pointed at a cushion that no longer exists — the worst failure mode this cluster has, because acting on it means working without authorization.
items.nextStep: Done. /ead-renewal-gap rebuilt around the repeal (before/after table, which cohort you are in, Form I-9 reality, E/L spouses authorised incident to status, rule status); /ead-processing-time FAQs and comparison rows corrected. Watch for a court restoring the extension — eadProcessingData.categories[].autoExtension is the flag to flip.

items.title: OCI guide stated two re-issue rules that do not exist, and three fees were wrong
items.detail: Official consulate guidance (CGI San Francisco; MHA) is that exactly ONE change needs a paid re-issue — a new passport obtained after completing 20 years of age — and everything else, including each new passport up to age 20 and one after 50, is a FREE portal upload within three months. /oci/renewal and the /oci hub told readers to re-issue at 50 (no such requirement) and to re-issue on every minor passport renewal (it is an upload). The fee config was wrong the same way against the published VFS USA schedule: re-issue $275 (actually $25 under Miscellaneous Services), passport update $100 (actually $25, and free via the portal), PIO-to-OCI free (actually $100). Quoting $275 for a $25 service is an 11x overstatement on the cluster's most common question, and the Cost Calculator inherited it.
items.nextStep: Done. Rules and fees corrected in src/lib/oci/config.ts, src/lib/ociGuides.ts, /oci and /oci/e-oci-card. The three-month upload deadline is now stated — it was missing entirely.

items.title: I-140 premium page said an RFE 'pauses' the clock; it stops and resets
items.detail: USCIS starts a NEW premium processing period when it receives the RFE or NOID response — days already run do not carry over. 'Pauses until you respond' implies the opposite and understates the cost of an RFE on a case someone paid $2,965 to accelerate. Also missing: that the period starts on receipt of a properly completed I-907 rather than on the I-140, that missing the deadline buys a fee refund rather than a decision, and that USCIS has suspended I-140 premium processing before.
items.nextStep: Done — corrected and expanded on /i140-premium-processing, plus a section on what paying cannot fix (priority date, I-485 queue, approval odds, the PERM steps ahead of it).

items.title: I-485 pages hedged on the medical-exam rule that has been settled since Dec 2024
items.detail: Since Dec 2, 2024 USCIS requires Form I-693 to be submitted WITH Form I-485, or the I-485 may be rejected. /i485-documents-checklist said the timing rule 'can change, so confirm current guidance', and /i485-timeline told readers a missing I-693 was 'the most common avoidable cause of an RFE at stage 5' — but the consequence is now rejection at filing, which is materially worse: no receipt number, no pending application, and no concurrently filed EAD or Advance Parole either. The validity rule was also missing (signed on/after Nov 1, 2023 = no expiry, but per the Jun 11, 2025 policy update valid only for the application it was filed with).
items.nextStep: Done. Both rules now stated with sources, in src/data/i485ProcessingData.ts (i693Rules) so the cluster shares one copy.
items.evidence: uscis.gov newsroom alerts on I-693 requirement and validity

items.title: Advance Parole page had no emergency route, which is the question people arrive with
items.detail: The page gave the 4–9 month queue and a travel warning. It did not mention emergency advance parole — the USCIS Contact Center to field-office appointment route that can produce a travel document in days — nor the published expedite criteria, nor what happens if the document lapses while you are abroad, nor the real trade-off for H-1B holders (re-entering on parole means you are a parolee, so the H-1B fallback if the I-485 is denied is what you are giving up).
items.nextStep: Done. All four added; the H-1B section is deliberately hedged to the practitioner position and points at an attorney.

items.title: Prevailing-wage pages explained the concept but not the mechanics
items.detail: /h1b-prevailing-wage (917 words) and /dol-wage-levels-explained (999 words) were the thinnest pages in the employment-GC clusters and omitted everything actionable: how to look up your own figure on the DOL FLAG wage search from the SOC code and worksite on your own LCA, the annual wage vintage that makes an old LCA figure legitimately lower than today's, the four permitted wage sources (OEWS, a CBA rate, a qualifying private survey, Davis-Bacon/SCA), what underpayment and unpaid benching actually mean, and the five-step level worksheet — including that supervisory duties add no point when supervision is customary for the occupation.
items.nextStep: Done. Both pages now carry the mechanics.
items.evidence: dol.gov ETA Prevailing Wage Determination Policy Guidance · flag.dol.gov

items.title: Return-to-India cluster covered every money question and no status question
items.detail: The biggest uncovered gap found in this pass. Grepping src/ for I-407, 're-entry permit' or 'abandonment of permanent resident' returned a single passing mention in a forms list. A green-card holder who spends a year in India can lose the status that lets them return (abandonment turns on intent, not only a day count), and one who formally hands it back can trigger the US exit tax — long-term resident at 8 of the last 15 tax years, then the $2m net worth / indexed net-income-tax / five-year certification tests, Form 8854, $10,000 penalty. Both are irreversible and neither belonged to any retirement article beneath the hub.
items.nextStep: Done. New section on /return-to-india, facts in src/data/returnToIndiaStatusData.ts with the indexed expatriation threshold carrying its tax year. Consider whether this deserves its own top-level page later — it is currently a hub section.

items.title: The two MoneyHub pages and /send-money-to-india had no content of their own
items.detail: /send-money-to-india (618 words), /india-property (870) and /return-to-india (957) were heroes, snapshots and card grids. /send-money-to-india cannot out-rank Wise or CompareRemit on rates and was not saying what they omit; the two MoneyHub pages were thinner than the articles beneath them.
items.nextStep: Done. MoneyHubConfig gained an optional deepDive slot (reusable, renders ahead of the link lists). /send-money-to-india now owns direction (TCS belongs to money leaving India), account choice (NRE repatriable, NRO not) and recipient taxability (the Rs 50,000 figure is a threshold, not an allowance). /india-property gets a four-situation router rather than new depth, because its cluster already owns the depth.

items.title: ledger:add silently swallowed space-separated flags into the item title
items.detail: CLAUDE.md documents `npm run ledger:add -- "..." --area content --sev high`, but scripts/audit/ledger-add.js only matched --flag=value, so the documented invocation put '--area content --sev high --next ...' into the title and filed the item as other/medium. The one failure mode a capture-first tool cannot afford, since the whole intake rule depends on it.
items.nextStep: Done — both forms parse now.

items.title: The NRE vs NRO article is 648 words and two headings, and other pages now cite it as the authority
items.detail: /articles/nre-nro-accounts-explained has exactly two H2s ('NRE vs NRO at a glance' and 'Choosing a transfer service') on what is the most consequential account decision an NRI makes — NRE balances are freely repatriable, NRO balances are not, and the choice is close to irreversible in practice. Three money-transfer articles and now the /send-money-to-india hub all route here for the detail, so it is load-bearing and thinner than its inbound links imply.
items.nextStep: Deepen to match the cluster: taxability of interest in each (NRE interest exempt for non-residents vs NRO fully taxable with TDS), the repatriation cap and Form 15CA/15CB on NRO, joint-holding rules, what happens to each account when you return to India and become resident again, and converting a resident account on becoming an NRI (there is a separate article for that last one — link, do not duplicate).

items.title: ~30 legacy /articles/* pages sit at 577-860 words with the same 5-10 heading skeleton
items.detail: The original starter article set (first-apartment-lease-guide, roth-ira-vs-traditional-nri, build-us-credit-score-from-zero, index-funds-for-beginners-nri, renters-insurance-explained and so on) is uniformly thin against a content tree whose cluster pages now run 2,000-14,000 words. They are indexable. Individually none is a competitor gap; collectively they are the weakest tier on the site and they dilute the topical signal of the hubs that link to them.
items.nextStep: Decide per topic rather than per page: consolidate a group into one deep guide with redirects (the credit trio, the insurance set), or deepen the two or three with real search demand and leave the rest as supporting pages. Do not bulk-expand all thirty — that is word count, not gap closure.

items.title: /topics and 14 /topics/* pages are 144-615 words, indexable, and out of the sitemap
items.detail: The legacy topic taxonomy (/topics/community at 144 words, /topics/stories 150, /topics/housing 184, up to /topics/taxes 615) is one H2 and a list of article cards each. They are not in any sitemap but nothing marks them noindex, which is the exact pattern the no-permutation-URLs rule calls out: sitemap omission does not stop indexing, noindex does. The hubs have long since superseded them as the entry points.
items.nextStep: Pick one: noindex the set and keep them as internal navigation, or redirect each into the hub that replaced it. Either is defensible; leaving them indexable and thin is not.

items.title: /calculators (476 words) and /education/articles (210) are thin and in the sitemap
items.detail: Both are navigational indexes rather than answer pages, so low word count is not automatically wrong — but /calculators is the entry point for the whole calculator tree and carries no framing at all, and /education/articles at 210 words is the thinnest page in the sitemap.
items.nextStep: Give /calculators a short 'which calculator for which decision' framing (the CalculatorHub pattern already exists for the leaf pages). For /education/articles, either fold it into /education or add real index framing.

items.title: Four employment-GC satellite pages are still on the ~1,000-word template
items.detail: This pass deepened /advance-parole-processing-time, /ead-renewal-gap, /i140-premium-processing, /i485-timeline, /i485-documents-checklist, /h1b-prevailing-wage and /dol-wage-levels-explained. Still on the thin template: /i140-processing-time (1,153 words), /pwd-processing-time (1,274), /h1b-perm-max-out-calculator (989) and /i485-timeline's sibling /eb2-eb3-priority-date-india (1,226). Their numbers are correct and centrally sourced; they are short on mechanics.

items.title: Record: clusters audited in Sep 2026 with no material gap found
items.detail: So the next pass does not re-audit them. Checked against live SERPs and competitor outlines, already at or above competitor depth: green card renewal (the 36-month I-90 receipt extension and the ADIT stamp are both covered, which is what competitors lead with), visa bulletin, Trump Account (9 pages), US government benefits (14,000 words), divorce and immigration (11,300), India investments (10,000), power of attorney for India (11,300), life insurance and IUL, visitor insurance (7 pages plus 6 calculators), education/F-1 (10 pages), Indian passport renewal, NVC (5 pages), India visa (7 pages), gold limit, H-1B lottery cluster. The H-1B, USCIS and visa-bulletin hubs are structurally sound; their gap is the verified-numbers backlog already tracked under fast-answer-coverage, not missing subtopics.
items.nextStep: Re-audit only when a rule changes or a SERP shifts. Treat this as a dated snapshot, not a permanent verdict.

items.title: 7 indiacode.nic.in statute citations return 404
items.detail: ledger:links now reports 8 dead citations, down from 10 after this pass repointed two (USCIS retired its automatic-EAD-extension page after the repeal; Study in the States retired /students/reinstatement). The remaining 7 are all indiacode.nic.in — both /handle/ and /bitstream/ forms, covering the Indian Stamp Act 1899, the Registration Act 1908, a 2025 act, and four handle IDs. Where a stable indiacode URL cannot be found, cite the relevant ministry's own copy instead.
